label: Week 1
goal: Get comfortable with the kit, motors, and first programs.

days.activity: Introduction to archaeology and project overview. Before students begin their projects, students will learn about the SPIKE Prime kit.
Students will continue to test how different LEGO parts can influence the way their robots move.
Students will learn about basic programming concepts.
Students will continue to learn how to program and will learn how to use a distance sensor.

label: Week 2
goal: Master gears, gyro, PID, and the color sensor.

days.activity: Students will learn about gears, gear ratio, torque, and speed.
Students will learn about the gyro sensor and will learn how to make their robots drive more straight.
Students will learn about PID and will learn how to improve their drive straight code.
Students will learn how to use the color sensor and will solve a maze.

label: Week 3
goal: Research a real problem and start prototyping with the engineering design process.

days.activity: Review final project, learn about archaeology, and research different ideas.
Learn about more archaeological issues and pick a problem to research.
Students will learn about the engineering design process and will begin to build their prototype.
Students will continue to use the engineering design process to improve their design.

label: Week 4
goal: Robotic arms, transforming robots, precision turns, and poster design.

days.activity: Students will learn how to build a robotic arm.
Students will learn how to build a transformative robot.
Students will learn how to make accurate turns using the gyro sensor and PID.
Students will begin to design their posters.

label: Week 5
goal: Improve prototypes, get feedback, and rehearse presentations.

days.activity: Students will continue to improve their prototypes and will continue to work on their prototypes.
Students will practice and show off their current design and receive feedback.
Students will make adjustments based on feedback.
Practice day — rehearse the full presentation with the team.

label: Week 6
goal: Final practice, presentation day, and the start of the new robot design.

days.activity: Final practice day.
Presentation Day / Release Day — show families the prototypes, posters, and robot skills.
Learn about the new robot design — a pin-less design.
Continue to work on the robot build and decide on a color scheme.

label: Week 7
goal: Starter code and competition strategy for the new robot.

days.activity: Build starter code file and begin to build strategy.

label: Week 8
goal: Wrap up the robot, strategy runs, and celebrate the summer.
